summary: David Bradley is a scholar of Buddhist studies and philosophy. He earned a B.A. (Hons) at King's College London (1972–1975) and studied at the University of Cambridge from 1975 to 1979.

David Brainerd Spooner (1879–1925) was an Indologist and archaeologist. Educated at Stanford, Tokyo, Sampurnanand, and Harvard (Ph.D. under Lanman, Pischel, and Marshall), he served in the Archaeological Survey of India from 1906, becoming Deputy Director-General in 1919.

David Brick is an Indologist who studied under Patrick Olivelle. He served on the editorial board of Anthem South Asian Normative Traditions Studies in 2012 and worked as a professor at Yale University (attested 2012–2018).

David Brown (1762–1812) was an Indology and religious studies scholar educated at Magdalene College, Cambridge (1782). He founded the Calcutta Auxiliary Bible Society and served as Provost of Fort William College from circa 1800 to 1807.

David Bubna-Litic works in Buddhist studies and management. He completed a PhD at Western Sydney University and served as Lecturer in Strategic Management and Responsible Business at the University of Technology Sydney (attested 2000).

David Burton, a Buddhist studies and philosophy scholar, earned his doctorate at the University of Bristol (1994–1997). He held posts at Keble College, Oxford (attested 2001) and Canterbury Christ Church University (attested 2010).

David Carpenter (born 1949) is a scholar in Indology and religious studies. He served as Associate Professor of the History of Religions at Saint Joseph's University (circa 1989) and Professor of Neurology at Washington University in St. Louis (2005).

David Dean Shulman (born 1949) is an Indology and religious studies scholar. Educated at Hebrew University and the University of London (Ph.D. under John Ralston Marr), he held multiple posts at Hebrew University from 1976 to 2017, including professor and director.

David Drewes is an Indology and Buddhist studies scholar who earned his PhD from the University of Virginia (2006). He taught at Virginia and Indiana University Bloomington before joining the University of Manitoba (attested 2008–2010).

David E. Cooper (born 1942) is a philosopher educated at Oxford. He lectured at the University of Oxford (1967), served as Professor of Philosophy at Durham University (1986–2008), and was a Distinguished International Visiting Professor at Peking University (2022).

David E. Riggs is a scholar of Japanology and Buddhist studies who earned his Ph.D. from UCLA. He taught at UC Santa Barbara, UIUC, and Hawaiʻi at Mānoa, and held research positions at Nichibunken (attested 2006) and Oberlin College (attested 2010).

David Faure (born 1947) is a sinologist and historian. Educated at the University of Hong Kong and Princeton (PhD 1976), he taught at Indiana University, St Antony's College, Oxford, and served as director at The Chinese University of Hong Kong (~2006–2022).

David Fiordalis, a scholar of Buddhist studies, Indology, and religious studies, earned his Ph.D. at the University of Michigan under Luis Oscar Gómez. He served as associate professor at Linfield University (attested 2017) and Research Editor for 84000 (2022).

David Friedman (1903–1984) was a scholar of Buddhist studies, Indology, and philosophy. Educated at Utrecht, Leiden, and Oxford, he held posts at Leiden University, University of Indonesia, SOAS, and the University of London.

David Gellner (born 1957) is a scholar of religious studies, Buddhist studies, and Indology. He has held appointments at the University of Oxford from 1988 to 2026, including serving as Emeritus Professor of Social Anthropology at Wolfson College.

David Germano is a Tibetologist and Buddhist studies scholar who completed his PhD at the University of Wisconsin-Madison in 1992. That same year, he became Associate Professor of Tibetan and Buddhist Studies at the University of Virginia.
David Gonsalez is a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies who studied under traditional teachers Lobsang Choephel, Lati Rinpoche, Kirti Tsenshab Rinpoche, and Denma Lochö Rinpoche.

David Goodman Mandelbaum (1911–1987) was an Indologist. He earned his Ph.D. at Yale under Edward Sapir, later holding academic posts at the University of Minnesota (circa 1938–1946) and the University of California, Berkeley (1946–1978).

David Gordon White (born 1953) is an Indology and religious studies scholar. After doctoral studies at the University of Chicago, he taught at the University of Virginia (1986–1996) and became J. F. Rowny Professor at UC Santa Barbara (1996).

David Higgins is a scholar of Tibetology, Buddhist studies, and philosophy. He has held research positions at the University of Vienna (attested 2015) and the International Institute for Buddhist Studies (attested 2026).
